title: Streaming Load Orchestrator: Stateless Virtual-user Factory for SSE/WSS Chat
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Build a horizontally scalable, stateless virtual-user factory (orchestrator) to generate SSE and WebSocket streaming chat/completion traffic at production-like scale. This ticket implements a new mode of our load bench that: (1) creates large numbers of short-lived and long-lived streaming sessions, (2) multiplexes many logical user conversations over a pool of worker connections, (3) injects realistic token production rates, and (4) measures both streaming-specific SLOs (time-to-first-token (TTFT), downstream token p95 latency, and sustained tokens/sec) and classic request p95s. The orchestrator must be language-agnostic (primary runners in Go + Node), emit Prometheus metrics and structured logs, and include a regression gate that compares targeted histograms (p95 token latency, TTFT) to a baseline stored in the metrics service. The system should allow per-test configuration for prefix caching, KV cache-warmup, batching window, and model variant fallback policies. Include chaos knobs (random connection churn, tail-bandwidth shaping) and a light-weight replay mode that can reproduce a user session trace for debugging.

Design constraints: keep worker processes stateless so they can be restarted/moved without losing virtual-user progress; use an external durable job queue to orchestrate session start/stop signals (Redis streams or SQS); avoid embedding heavy client-side language models; simulate token emissions using recorded token-rate distributions. Emphasis on minimizing client-side resource usage so a single machine can simulate thousands of logical users.

Deliverables: code for orchestrator and clients, Prometheus dashboards with regression alerts, a short runbook for running peak tests in Dedicated and Hosted environments, example config files for 50k, 100k, and 200k concurrent logical sessions, and a PR with integration tests that validate the p95 gate logic.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator can spin up 50k logical streaming sessions using <= 120 worker processes on a 48vCPU/192GB machine (stateless workers)
Token throughput: sustained >= 250k tokens/sec across the cluster in the 50k-session profile, with measured tokens/sec exposed to Prometheus
p95 streaming token latency and TTFT are captured as Prometheus histograms and can be compared to a stored baseline; regression gate flags when p95 degrades > 12%
Replay mode reproduces a recorded session end-to-end with identical token boundaries 95% of the time
Chaos knobs (connection churn, 5–200 ms downstream jitter, simulated packet loss 0–5%) execute and produce expected failures without crashing the orchestrator
Integration tests and a demo job (config + dashboard) are merged to runtime-1.20 branch
test_scenarios: Steady long-lived sessions: 10k sessions with average 120s duration, token-rate distribution from corpus A
Burst start: ramp 0 -> 30k sessions over 2 minutes with prefix-cache cold start
Mixed short/long: 40% short (10s), 60% long (90s) to exercise KV cache behavior
High token-rate users: 2% of sessions emit tokens at 5x mean rate to create tail load
Regional failover: simulate region A degraded and fallback to region B while preserving session continuity
Replay of a production trace captured during a major outage to validate deterministic replay
observability: Expose metrics via Prometheus and a /debug/metrics endpoint
Structured JSON logs for every logical session start/stop and connection error
Automatic generation of a Grafana dashboard template for tokens/sec and TTFT
Alert rule: test.regression_score == 1 triggers PagerDuty with link to test run and baseline diff
Trace snippets (Jaeger) for representative slow sessions captured via sampling
implementation_plan: Week 1: Proto: stateless worker binary that opens N SSE and WSS connections and emits token streams from a synthetic generator
Week 2: Orchestrator with job queue and multiplexing logic; wire up Prometheus metrics
Week 3: Chaos injection, replay mode, and regional routing/fallback simulator
Week 4: Build regression gate comparator, dashboards, integration tests, and runbook
Week 5: Run large-scale smoke test in Dedicated (50k sessions) and tune kernels/connection pooling
